binary: manhunt.exe (2004 retail build, PE32/i386, no ASLR, ImageBase 0x00400000)
summary: Fully drivable unattended, except moving the character. Self-launch works but stops at an ANSI Win32 launcher dialog that must be BM_CLICKed. The frontend IS drivable: the game reads the DirectInput MOUSE, and proxy-side synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2 moves the cursor, moves the menu highlight, and activates entries -- menu to live gameplay, unattended. The in-game camera responds to the same route. What does NOT work is character movement: no scancode tried has moved him, and the keys this game binds have never been read out of the binary. IMPORTANT: two harness defects made this game look completely input-proof until 2026-09-10 and every input finding before that date is withdrawn -- see input.harness_traps.

measured_paths.claim: The game polls the DirectInput MOUSE on the order of 20,000 times a second, with cbData = 20 (DIMOUSESTATE2). It also calls GetDeviceState on the KEYBOARD device, but with cbData = 0, which cannot return key state, and that count freezes once gameplay starts. GetDeviceData is never called on either device.
measured_paths.numbers: launch 2, mid-gameplay: SysMouse state=22,708,637 cbData=20; SysKeyboard state=12,981 cbData=0; GetDeviceData=0 on both
measured_paths.how: per-device counters in the project's own d3d8 proxy (input.c), after the per-device hooking fix
measured_paths.implication: Inject into GetDeviceState on the MOUSE device. Why the keyboard is polled with cbData = 0 is UNEXPLAINED and is the open question -- log the first ~20 keyboard calls with cbData, lpvData, hr and the RETURN ADDRESS to learn who is calling it.

working.route: Proxy-side synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2 (relative deltas + buttons) added into the buffer returned by GetDeviceState on the SysMouse device, driven by the manhunt_vr_input.txt script file
working.result: main menu -> SELECT SCENE -> BORN AGAIN -> live gameplay, entirely unattended; camera pans ~90 degrees on one move in gameplay
working.how_to_get_it_right: Movement axes are RELATIVE and the game polls ~20,000x/sec, so a delta added on every poll is 100x the intended motion. Hand movement over in TICKS at a real-mouse report rate (~8 ms / 125 Hz), spread over a requested duration. Buttons are the opposite -- a LEVEL, ORed on every poll, because a button missed for one frame is a dropped click.

calibration_dev_pc.note: Measured from a controlled 100-count move away from both window edges. The engine's known horizontal stretch is 1.39x (a 1.28 aspect rendered into a 1.7778 backbuffer), which is suggestively close but not proven to be the same number.
calibration_dev_pc.warning: Moves that reach a window edge CLAMP silently and make the rate look like 0.70 px/count. Calibrate away from the edges.

working.route: A synthetic left click during the intro credits
working.result: main menu reached ~28 s after Play instead of ~180 s -- appears to skip the credits
working.caveat: n=1, and the credits do end on their own. 28 s against 180 s is a large gap, but this is not yet a controlled test.

disproved.route: Proxy-side synthetic DirectInput KEYBOARD state, with the keyboard device's vtable genuinely hooked
disproved.result: no effect; cursor did not move and the highlight did not change. The keyboard device is called with cbData = 0 and never returns key state.

disproved.route: SendInput scancodes W (0x11, 6 s) and Up arrow (0x48 + KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, 4 s), with the struct size FIXED and the return value confirmed as 1 down / 1 up
disproved.result: scene unchanged; the character did not move
disproved.scope_warning: This is a correct negative for TWO scancodes, in one spot, in one level. It is NOT 'the keyboard does nothing'. The keys this game actually binds have never been read out of the binary or its config.

disproved.route: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-10: all SendInput results recorded before 2026-09-10b (keyboard scancodes, absolute mouse move + click, relative mouse move)
disproved.result: Not evidence. SendInput was returning 0 with GetLastError = 87 and inserting zero events -- see input.harness_traps. These were never tests.

disproved.route: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-10: 'the white arrow beside the menu entries is menu art and never moves'
disproved.result: It is the CURSOR. It moves exactly as one under synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2, and the menu highlight follows whichever entry it is over. It never moved before because nothing was ever delivered to the mouse.

harness_traps.trap: Only the FIRST DirectInput device was hooked
harness_traps.detail: The proxy guarded its vtable hooks with a single global flag. This game creates SysMouse first and SysKeyboard second, and the two devices do NOT share a vtable (mouse 0x742395F4, keyboard 0x74239570, different real function pointers). The keyboard was therefore never instrumented, and the recorded 'GetDeviceState = 11,917,105 on the mouse, 0 on the keyboard' was an uninstrumented device reporting nothing -- not a measurement. Synthetic keyboard state was likewise never installed in the keyboard's vtable, so 'the keyboard route does not work' was untested.
harness_traps.fix: Hook every distinct vtable, keep the original function pointers PER vtable, and publish each record before patching its slots.

harness_traps.trap: SendInput never sent anything (this one is universal, not Manhunt-specific)
harness_traps.detail: The PowerShell harness declared the INPUT struct as 28 bytes -- the 32-bit layout -- while running in 64-bit PowerShell, where INPUT is 40 bytes (DWORD type, 4 bytes of padding, then a 32-byte union). Every call returned 0 with GetLastError = 87 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and inserted ZERO events. Nothing checked the return value, so it read as 'the game ignores synthetic input'.
harness_traps.fix: Always assert SendInput's return value equals the number of events passed, and log GetLastError when it does not. A silently failing input API and an ignored input API are indistinguishable from outside.

untried: Read the game's real key bindings out of the binary or its settings, rather than guessing scancodes.
Log the first ~20 SysKeyboard GetDeviceState calls with cbData, lpvData, hr and the caller's return address, to explain the cbData = 0 anomaly.
A gamepad, via the game's GAME_CONTROL_TYPE setting -- never tried.

entry_points.name: steam-launch
entry_points.notes: Reaches the launcher dialog in roughly 20-25 s. The proxy DLL loads and patches within 0.6 s of process start.

entry_points.name: launcher-dialog
entry_points.how: A top-level window titled MANHUNT owns a small dialog ('Manhunt launcher', ~414x346) with Play / Quit buttons and video settings. Enumerate its child windows and send BM_CLICK (0x00F5) to the child whose text is 'Play'.
entry_points.hazard: Read child window text with GetWindowTextA, NOT GetWindowTextW. The dialog is ANSI, so the W variant returns only the first character - 'P' for Play, 'Q' for Quit - which reads exactly like 'no Play button found'. Same for GetClassNameA ('B' instead of 'BUTTON').

entry_points.name: skip-the-frontend
entry_points.how: Edit initscripts/FRONTEND/settings.txt with the game CLOSED: set SKIP_MENU 1 and START_LEVEL 0 (the built-in 'Test level'). Launch, click Play in the launcher dialog, then wait ~50 s.
entry_points.result: lands directly in live 3D - real in-engine rendering with HUD, crosshair and subtitles - with no frontend involved. Ran 3 min 30 s before hitting a separate, understood crash (spline table, see hazards).
entry_points.notes: This is currently the ONLY way to reach a running game unattended, because the frontend cannot be driven. START_LEVEL 1 (the first real level, 'Doorway Into Hell') loads too and shows its title card, but overflows the spline table sooner.

routes.how: BM_CLICK (0x00F5) the child button whose GetWindowTextA is 'Play'
a synthetic left click (MB 0) -- reached the menu in ~28 s instead of the ~180 s the credits take on their own
routes.warning: The credits also end unprompted. Treat this as a strong lead, not a settled skip, until it is run again.

routes.how: Move the cursor onto SELECT SCENE with synthetic mouse deltas, CAPTURE and VERIFY the highlight, left-click; then move onto the first scene thumbnail, verify again, click. Reaches live gameplay in about a minute.
routes.supersedes: the 2026-09-10 entry that recorded this route as UNSOLVED
routes.hazard: QUIT is the bottom entry of the main menu. Never blind key-count or blind-move past it -- move, capture, verify the highlight, and only then click.

routes.how: synthetic mouse X deltas; ~900 counts pans roughly 90 degrees

settings_file.notes: Plain text, read at startup only - edit with the game closed. Useful keys: START_LEVEL (0 = Test level, 1-n = real levels), SKIP_MENU (1 = boot straight into START_LEVEL), GAME_CONTROL_TYPE, GAME_CONTROL_INVERT_Y, FX_MODE. There is also a 'Frontend disable (FOR DEBUG ONLY!)' option.

registry.notes: Device / Mode / Index. Mode is a RenderWare video-mode index handed verbatim to RwEngineSetVideoMode. Deleting the Video key makes the game recreate its defaults. On the dev PC, mode index 0 enumerated as 1920x1080 WINDOWED (the desktop resolution).

capture.method: BitBlt from the screen DC (Graphics.CopyFromScreen over the window rect), after SetForegroundWindow
capture.warning: Do not use PrintWindow - it serves stale DWM-cached frames when the game stops presenting, with no error. This is a portfolio-wide rule, not specific to Manhunt.
capture.notes: The game window is a normal top-level window; the proxy resizes its client area to 800x600. Several invisible top-level windows share the PID, so pick the largest VISIBLE one.

hazards.what: Spline table overflow crash -- RELOCATED, and it held for one level
hazards.detail: The spline (camera path) loader wrote into a fixed 100-entry table at 0x007134F4 whose count sits in the word immediately after the last slot (0x00713684), with no bounds check; the 101st spline overwrote the count and the next iteration faulted at 0x00471FFB. Clamping the count (SPLINEGUARD) removed that crash but only MOVED the fault to a memcpy into a null spline at 0x0061166A. The project's proxy now RELOCATES the table to a 1024-slot buffer (SPLINERELOC) after verifying that the base literal occurs exactly six times in the whole image and that nothing reaches the table by a computed base. A full real level then ran ~8 minutes with no overflow and no crash. NOT yet closed: that level was reached through the menu, and the original crash happened on a SKIP_MENU DIRECT START, which has not been re-run since the relocation.

Sixteen call sites in the retail exe run leftover anti-tamper checks that deliberately sabotage the game (stuck gates, item/useable crashes, broken saving, ammo drain). The project's proxy patches all sixteen at runtime, first try on every launch that carried them. Confirmed firing IN GAMEPLAY for the first time on 2026-09-10: Broken Health 1, Broken SaveGame EntityData, and Help Text Crash (the last roughly every 5-8 s), all returning the repaired value with the game continuing normally. Without the proxy, expect the documented bug cluster.

The exe is packed at rest by a SecuROM protector stub and external debugger attach fails ('Could not open process'). All static analysis must be done against a dump of the unpacked image; all patching must be done in-process from an injected DLL.

hazards.what: Window-edge clamping makes mouse calibration lie
hazards.detail: A synthetic mouse move that reaches a window edge stops there silently. Two probe moves that both clamped made the cursor rate look like 0.70 px/count when it is 1.87 (X) and 1.36 (Y). Calibrate with a move that starts and ends well away from every edge.

process_exit.how: SendMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE) to the game's visible top-level window
process_exit.notes: Exits cleanly, no taskkill needed. Historically, once the SecuROM bug cluster has been hit in gameplay the process can become unresponsive and need a force-kill; that has not recurred since the DRM patches went in, but n is small.
